item.title: Iranian missiles could have hit DC from Venezuela before Trump move, Burgum warns
item.summary: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum revealed that Iran could have hit Washington, D.C., and other U.S. cities through proxies in Venezuela had the Trump administration not intervened.

item.title: 'Mormon Wives' star claims estranged husband lived double life with escorts, sex parties
item.summary: "Secret Lives of Mormon Wives" star Jessi Draper claims estranged husband Jordan Ngatikaura contacted an escort service during their marriage in a bombshell interview.

item.title: White House warns Iran against balking at deal: Trump ready to 'unleash hell'
item.summary: President Donald Trump is prepared to "unleash hell" if Iran balks at a deal with the U.S., White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said Wednesday.

item.title: 290 US service members injured during Operation Epic Fury against Iran, CENTCOM says
item.summary: Around 290 U.S. service members have been injured during Operation Epic Fury, a CENTCOM spokesperson said, and more than 255 of those have already returned to duty.

item.title: Taylor Frankie Paul under investigation for third alleged domestic violence incident with ex-boyfriend
item.summary: "Secret Lives of Mormon Wives" Taylor Frankie Paul is under investigation for a third alleged domestic violence incident involving ex-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen.

item.title: DAVID MARCUS: Why are we letting foreign foes use X payouts to wage war against us?
item.summary: X's proposed monetization changes could stop foreign bot farms from funding divisive U.S. creators, but Elon Musk has delayed the policy for review.

item.title: Iran-linked influence campaign pushes anti-Israel messaging disguised as US voices: report
item.summary: Foreign accounts allegedly mimic American voices online, with Argyle research claiming 60% of Operation Epic Fury discourse originates outside the U.S.

item.title: GREGG JARRETT: Jury blames Meta, Google for teen harm—but appeal could crush case
item.summary: An L.A. jury awarded $3 million in a child social media addiction case, but Section 230 and First Amendment protections may doom the verdict on appeal.

item.title: White House unleashes on Raskin for clinging to 'deranged' Jack Smith 'lies' in latest Trump docs flare-up
item.summary: The White House and DOJ are pushing back against Rep. Jamie Raskin's letter alleging Trump mishandled classified documents, calling the accusations baseless and a political stunt.

item.title: Loyola student newspaper apologizes for calling suspected murderer of Sheridan Gorman an illegal immigrant
item.summary: The Loyola Phoenix apologized after an Instagram post called Sheridan Gorman's alleged killer an "illegal immigrant," citing conflicts with AP style.
